source.title: Efficient Proximal Mapping of the 1-path-norm of Shallow Networks
source.authors: Fabian Latorre; Paul Rolland; Nadav Hallak; V. Cevher

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that blocks extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Its own experiments show that 1-path-norm regularization does not consistently improve clean test error while promoting robustness; the paper also refines the interpretation of a cited generalization-measure result, but does not test the mapped versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates clean and adversarial test error under regularization schemes, but it does not report the training-versus-test error gap, random-label fitting, width sweeps, optimizer generalization comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout effects, sharpness measurements, or removal of memorized examples. Clean test-error results under regularization bear on V6 only insofar as they measure the outcome of an explicit regularizer; they do not evaluate dropout. Proximal-SGD versus SGD loss convergence and sparsity are not generalization-gap outcomes. Cited claims about path-norm correlation and spectral product bounds are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study tests path-norm regularization, optimization, sparsity, and adversarial robustness, none of which measures V1–V8. Its discussion of generalization correlations cites prior work and does not test magnitude-aware sharpness. Comparing proximal SGD with SGD on regularized training loss does not test V4, and clean test error under path-norm regularization does not test dropout in V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors derive an efficiently computable proximal mapping and a path-norm upper bound on the Lipschitz constant under their activation assumptions. Their experiments report faster objective convergence and sparse iterates with proximal SGD, a favorable robustness–accuracy trade-off relative to L1 regularization, only a slight robustness advantage over layer-wise constraints, and difficulty combining accuracy with sparsity on KMNIST.
record.recipe_differences: Shallow networks trained with proximal-gradient regularization to study optimization, sparsity, and robustness-accuracy trade-offs; not the memorization or generalization-gap methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset difficulty and regularization choice affect the reported clean-error and robustness trade-off; the authors note a difficulty on KMNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 7.2 and E.2 compare clean and PGD adversarial test errors under path-norm, L1, and layer-wise regularization. Path-norm regularization has only a slight reported robustness advantage over layer-wise constraints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Path-norm regularization can trade clean accuracy for adversarial robustness in shallow image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 7.1 reports that proximal SGD reaches lower regularized training loss than plain SGD after 20 epochs and produces sparse iterates; path-norm regularization struggles to combine accuracy and sparsity on KMNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Proximal optimization of nonsmooth regularizers can improve objective convergence and induce sparsity, with dataset-dependent accuracy costs.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119 (2020)
record.problems: The experiments use shallow networks with 200 hidden neurons, 20 epochs, batch size 100, and six random initializations per parameter combination. Reported figures show error trends without numeric values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. Results do not measure the train-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows for the mapped versions: the reported optimization loss, sparsity, and adversarial robustness outcomes do not measure those versions' named behaviours. Clean test-error figure results are under path-norm, L1, or layer-wise regularization and do not test dropout or another listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with generalization on natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across dropout strengths, training-set sizes, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T5 classification to discusses/T6. There are no rows to repair and no missing results bearing on the listed versions. Input-space adversarial robustness is distinct from V7's weight-perturbation sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and architectural-bias comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and their held-out performance.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including training-set-size and overfitting regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing highly memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
